execution.description: Built the Challenge-neutral sheet and adapter types and the F0-F4 cost calculator for JAX and PyTorch, with battery's adapter as the first instance.

expected: Compile one training step on the pinned image, read XLA's FLOP estimate, and multiply by steps.
observed: A Challenge's training code rarely exposes one step: battery jits the whole training loop as one scan, and XLA's cost analysis counts a loop body once whatever its trip count (a 1-, 10- and 100-step scan reported the same FLOPs). Capturing the jitted program the Challenge's own code builds, then compiling each scan body alone and counting it per iteration, gives a per-step cost with no change to pinned implementation code. The default battery recipe costs about 479M FLOPs per step, near 6 x parameters x cases per update.
keep: Measure the program the Challenge's own code compiles; never re-implement its training to cost it.
A cost read from XLA counts each loop body once: expand loops by their trip count, and refuse loops without one.
Change only the measured quantity when measuring a recipe: a changed setting can switch the recipe onto another training path.
change: The study fits each backend's conversion to seconds separately: XLA counts element-wise operations, PyTorch's counter counts matrix products.
